claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you claiming Child Benefit for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for just one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So we're assessing eligibility for your son, Alex.

Now, to help determine if you're eligible, I need to know:

**How old is Alex, and does he currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 20 and yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I need to check the eligibility criteria to ensure I'm giving you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the eligibility rules that Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16 or over only if they're in approved education or training and are under 20 years old.

I need to ask you a bit more about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training? For example, is he at university, college, doing an apprenticeship, or involved in other approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided, I have what I need to assess your eligibility.

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16. For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify only if the child is under 20 and staying in approved education or training.

Since Alex is 20 years old and is not in approved education or training, he falls outside the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**. 

The reason is that Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in approved education or training. Child Benefit is only payable for children over 16 if they are under 20 and staying in approved education or training. Since Alex doesn't meet these conditions, he is no longer eligible for Child Benefit.

If Alex were to return to approved education or training before his 20th birthday, you would be able to claim Child Benefit for him again during that period. If you have any other questions or if circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
